items.new_text: The same Meta message creates a step only once (migration 0014).
Store the ProcessHttp cursor separately to retain every executed position.

`fluxo` or `roteador`.

This is the source platform's `template` (`builder` and `master`), shown on its portal card. A router is the SAME bot without its own content: it references other bots and chooses where the conversation goes. That is why this is a column rather than a new table.
A silently failing workflow is worse than no workflow.

Contact photo URL from the source platform's `imageUri`, used by the portal card to draw the avatar.

It is genuinely optional: the source wraps upload in `try/catch`, reporting only to the console and allowing creation to continue. Migration 0020.
A structured query checked against the tenant data dictionary. Never raw client SQL; the server imposes `tenant_id`.

Short identifier derived from the name (`name.toLowerCase()` in the source). It appears in the contact URL there (`/application/detail/{shortName}`), which is why the name must begin with a letter. There is no unique index; uniqueness is checked on `nome`. Migration 0020.

Mirror of the tenant CRM (Twenty) `objectMetadata`; see migration 0015.

`codigo` maps to `nameSingular`, `rotulo` to `labelSingular`, and the remaining columns follow Twenty property names. Rows with `twentyId` came from synchronization; rows without it were declared manually in the local CRM.
The item disappeared from Twenty. Keep its row so a referring block can report the missing item.

This is operational data, not just documentation: the query language reads it to decide what is allowed.

Mirror of Twenty `fieldMetadata`: `codigo` is `name`, `rotulo` is `label`, and `tipo` is the literal `type` (`TEXT`, `CURRENCY`, `RELATION`, ...). `options`, `defaultValue`, `settings`, and `relation` retain the exact Metadata API shape.

Outbound webhook authentication follows the source's "Configurações de autenticação" (`referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-integracoes-webhook.md`: switch and OAuth 2.0), plus Basic authentication required by the task although absent from the source. Migration 0036.

Contact description from the source platform's "Editar Fluxo" `description` at `/configurations/basic`.

It is optional (`<textarea>` lacks `required`); when present it must contain 2-160 characters (`ng-minlength="2"`, `ng-maxlength="160"`). The database `check` enforces the maximum, the only bound it can enforce alone; the `api` enforces the minimum. Migration 0022.
Basic-auth password, encrypted at rest by `@pipe/db/segredo`.
OAuth 2.0 token URL (`client_credentials`), validated like the webhook URL: HTTPS and no private network.

Custom headers as `[{ chave, valor }]`. Never include signature-reserved headers (`content-type`, `x-pipe-signature`, `x-pipe-timestamp`, `x-pipe-delivery`) or `authorization`: the write rule in `dominio/gestao/integracoes.ts` rejects them before this column, so no database `check` is needed for that rule.

"Utilizar o contexto do Roteador" (`builder:useTunnelOwnerContext`): as a router service, variables belong to the (router, contact) pair and are shared with other services that enable this option. Otherwise they belong only to this flow. Migration 0024.

Contact settings without a dedicated home: currently "Tela de Boas-vindas" (`{ boasVindas: { ativo, mensagem, textoBotao } }`) and "Menu Persistente" (`{ menuPersistente: { itens: [{texto,link}] } }`) from `/configurations/welcome` and `/configurations/persistentMenu`. A missing key means never configured. Migration 0031.

These few fields describe one screen each and have no history of their own, unlike `fluxo_versao.global`, which belongs to a published VERSION. A column stores the contact's current snapshot like `nome` and `descricao`; a separate table is unnecessary.
